guide.summary: Lets an alga swim slowly toward brighter light.
guide.biology: Many real algae swim toward light using a small whip-like tail and a light-sensing spot.
guide.rules: Costs 0.02 energy per second while carried. Gives a base speed of 0.15 cells per second and light sensing up to 2 cells, which the motility and sensing loci then adjust. It moves only when a nearby cell is at least 0.01 brighter; walls, barriers and habitat limits still apply. While swimming it pays 0.10 × (0.5 + g)² energy per second, where g is its motility investment from 0 to 1, instead of the usual cost per cell moved. If the module is lost it stays where it is.
guide.example: Give Sunbeads light seeking in a dish with one bright spot and watch whether they gather there.
